chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah from Aban from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about selling the pasture when it is dry, so the man directs his water to it, irrigates the land, and waters the grass, and he is the one who dug the river, and the water belongs to him, so he plants in it whatever he wishes. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the water belongs to him, let him plant in it whatever he wishes, and sell it for whatever he likes.'
He said: 'And I asked him about selling the harvest of wheat and barley and the rest of the harvests. He said: It is permissible, so let him sell it if he wishes.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on selling pasture land and agricultural harvests?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the property rights of the water owner (*malik al-ma'*), establishing that ownership of the irrigation source grants full autonomy over the resulting pasture (*kal'*) and crops. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that agricultural produce is a direct extension of the owner's capital investment in water, thereby validating the commercial sale of both the land's yield and the harvested grains like wheat and barley. It reflects the practical economic norms of early Islamic society where water scarcity made water rights synonymous with land rights.
